readmeExcerpt:
Orca

中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Español · Français · Português · Türkçe · Русский

The AI Orchestrator for 100x builders.
Run Claude Code, Codex, and any other coding agent in parallel, each in its own worktree. Chat or terminal, on your laptop or in the cloud, with diffs, a browser, and a CLI in one app.

Download Orca

## Features
### Chat or Terminal Run any agent in Chat UI or as the raw CLI, and move a conversation between the two without losing context. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/agents/native-chat)
### Orchestrate Agents Hand a big task to one agent. It splits the work, starts worker agents in their own workspaces, and brings their results back to you. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/orchestration)
### Run Anywhere Pair a Remote Orca Server, work on any SSH host, or give a worktree its own cloud VM. Your agents keep running when your laptop sleeps. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/ways-to-run)
### Mobile App Pair Orca with the mobile app to get pinged when an agent needs you, reply in chat, and keep work moving on any of your machines when you are away from your desk. [iOS App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/orca-ide/id6766130217) · [Android APK](https://orca.dev/download/android) · [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/mobile)
### Review AI Output Review diffs, leave notes on exact changed lines, and send focused feedback back to an agent. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/review/annotate-ai-diff)
### Git Integration Draft commit messages and pull requests from the diff, then send failing checks or PR review comments back to an agent to fix. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/review/commit-push)
### Parallel Worktrees Quickly split tasks into isolated environments, so multiple agents can work side by side without interfering with each other. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/model/worktrees)
### Design Mode Click any element in Orca's browser to copy its HTML, styles, and selector, then paste it into your agent's chat. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/browser/design-mode)
### GitHub & Linear, Native See your GitHub and Linear tasks in one place, and start a workspace for each when you're ready to build. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/review/linear)
### Orca CLI Anything you can do in Orca, your agents can do too: create worktrees, start workers, drive the browser and desktop apps, and schedule automations, all from the command line. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/overview)
### Plugins Themes, editors, languages, and panels from the community, installed in a click. [Browse plugins →](https://orca.dev/plugins)
### Split Anything Put agents, terminals, browsers, and diffs side by side in split panes shaped to the task. [Docs →](https://orca.dev/docs/model/tabs-panes-splits)
**Also in the box:** - **[Drag Files to Agents](https://orca.dev/docs/editing/file-explorer)**: drag files from the explorer, or images from your desktop, straight into an agent's prompt. - **[Jump Anywhere](https://orca.dev/docs/model/quick-open)**: one shortcut jumps to any workspace or tab across every repo and host. - **[Rich Previews](https://orca.dev/docs/editing/viewers)**: open images, PDFs, and Markdown right in the workspace, next to the agent that made them. - **[Mobile Emulator](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/overview#mobile-emulator)**: run an iOS Simulator or Android emulator beside your agent, and let it tap, type, and check its own work. - **[Dictation](https://orca.dev/docs/settings#voice)**: press a shortcut and talk. Orca types what you say into the agent's prompt or terminal. - **[Usage & Accounts](https://orca.dev/docs/agents/usage-tracking)**: see how much of your agent limits you've used and when they reset, and switch accounts without logging out. - **[Automations](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/automations)**: schedule prompts to run on any repo: nightly dependency bumps, weekly triage, flaky-test sweeps. - **[Computer Use](https://orca.dev/docs/cli/computer-use)**: when there's no CLI or API, agents can see and drive desktop apps and external browsers. - **And many, many more**: we ship daily, so this list is perpetually behind. The [changelog](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases) is the real feature list. --- ## Supported Agents Works with **any CLI agent** — if it runs in a terminal, it runs in Orca.

Claude Code   Codex   Grok   Cursor   GitHub Copilot   Muse

aiSummary.oneLiner: An AI orchestrator enabling developers to run multiple autonomous coding agents simultaneously in parallel worktrees.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Orca functions as a sophisticated Agent Development Environment (ADE) designed specifically to orchestrate fleets of parallel AI coding agents. It wraps multiple independent sessions, allowing users to concurrently run models like Claude Code, Codex, or Pi within their own isolated git worktrees. Available seamlessly across native desktop, mobile, and VPS environments, Orca centralizes task management and provides extremely fast, WebGL-rendered Ghostty-class terminals to monitor output. It effectively multiplies a single developer's bandwidth by allowing them to supervise and steer multiple autonomous refactoring or development tasks simultaneously.
keyFeatures: Parallel orchestration: Expertly manages multiple autonomous coding agents running simultaneously in completely isolated git worktrees.
Cross-platform support: Provides native applications for desktop environments, mobile devices, and remote headless Linux servers.
High-performance terminals: Includes extremely fast, WebGL-rendered terminals with highly persistent scrollback for monitoring agent output.
Mobile supervision: Includes a dedicated mobile companion app to actively monitor agent progress and send follow-up commands remotely.
Subscription flexibility: Allows users to easily integrate their own provider API keys to directly manage inference costs across the fleet.

useCases.title: Remote supervision
useCases.description: Developers start a complex, long-running agent task on their desktop and monitor its progress from their phone during a commute.

useCases.title: Distributed testing
useCases.description: QA leads spin up parallel agents in isolated worktrees to simultaneously write and execute test suites against different microservices.

useCases.title: Cost optimization
useCases.description: Power users utilize custom API keys within the orchestrator to heavily manage and optimize the financial cost of running multiple agents.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Power users, tech leads, and highly ambitious developers aiming to drastically scale their output by orchestrating multi-agent workflows. It is ideal for teams comfortable managing complex, distributed development environments.

**Previous release: [1.4.257](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/tag/v1.4.257)** — Smoother long chats, saved browser feedback and better dictation.

## Smoother workspaces, restored phone scrolling & Copilot Chat ✨

Orca 1.4.258 cuts pauses when opening large workspace collections, moving windows and changing the layout. Local usage updates do less work on the process handling your keystrokes, helping Chat UI and terminal users keep working while usage refreshes.

- 📱 **Scroll phone chats again:** On chat pages served by the desktop, swipe through messages and sideways through wide code blocks. Pinch with two fingers to resize chat text without zooming the whole page.
- 💬 **Use GitHub Copilot in Chat:** Choose **Launch chat** to stream replies, inspect tool output and review file diffs in a conversation you can reopen after restarting Orca.
- ⌨️ **Start Pi with your chosen model and thinking level:** The terminal launcher applies your model choice and offers reasoning effort before you send the first prompt.
- 🗂️ **Add projects with fewer steps:** Browse a folder, clone a URL or create a project directly from **Add project**. Switch machines inside the menu; from **New w

**Previous release: [1.4.256](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/tag/v1.4.256)** — Easier on-device dictation setup and earlier long-chat performance improvements.

## Smoother long chats, saved feedback and better dictation ✨

Orca 1.4.257 reduces freezes when several long Chat UI conversations stream at once. If you keep multiple agents working in conversations with a lot of history, this update cuts the work Orca does as their replies arrive.

- 🌐 **Keep your browser feedback across restarts:** Unsent text notes on pages in Orca’s browser now return after a reload or restart. Closing a tab with unsent notes asks before discarding them, so you can leave feedback and come back to it later. Agents running on your desktop can read those notes with `orca tab annotations` before you press Send.
- 🎙️ **Give yourself time to think while dictating:** In **Settings → Voice → Input → Stop After Silence**, choose 30 seconds, one minute, two minutes or Off. Dictation can wait through a longer pause while you compose a message or terminal command. The same settings page adds a **Test** button to record and play back your microphone, with a transcript when your speech model is ready.

## Smoother performance, easier dictation, saved phone drafts & clearer workspace controls ✨

Long chats stay more responsive while agents stream tool output, reasoning and subagent work, with less background processing during terminal and tab updates. This update also makes dictation easier to set up and use and makes agents and cloud workspaces easier to manage. Phone-specific improvements below require the matching phone app update.

- 🎙️ **Dictate with less setup:** Voice settings suggests an on-device model for your language and offers one setup button. Add personal or repository vocabulary, remove filler words, and use Auto mode to hold the shortcut or tap to toggle. On-device dictation inserts phrases as you pause, and you can dictate into fields in Orca's browser.
- 📱 **Pick up where you left off:** Chats show their saved recent messages after a phone relaunch while reconnecting. Commit messages, PR descriptions, comments, review notes, tasks and new-workspace drafts survive closing the app.
- ⌨️ **More control from your phone:** The terminal key row gains Shift, Ctrl and Alt latches and an optional Smart rail with agent actions. A floating dictation pill lets you keep sp

## Faster session search, agents on your phone & smoother chat switching ✨

We shipped two releases in quick succession: 1.4.254 yesterday and 1.4.255 today. See the [1.4.254 release notes](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/tag/v1.4.254) for Git Graph, chat forks, on-device phone dictation, more resilient mobile work, and pairing and trust improvements.

A little less waiting, a little more flow. This update makes large session histories easier to search, brings your agents together on your phone, and smooths out the everyday work of switching accounts, models and workspaces.

- ⚡ **Find past work without slowing down:** Session History searches run off the app’s main thread, keep results visible while you type, and show your last list immediately after a restart while it refreshes. Search also works on SSH and remote-server hosts.
- 📱 **Your agents, together on your phone:** A new Agents tab lists agents across your connected desktops. Mark them read or clear them from the list, with activity status supplied by the desktop. Saved task lists and host labels appear sooner when you reopen the app.
- 💬 **Keep your chat moving:** Switching Codex accounts moves your open Codex

## Git Graph, on-phone dictation & side questions in chat ✨

- 🌳 **See the whole repository:** A new Git Graph tab shows local and remote branches and tags, with each commit's details and changed files. Folder workspaces now get Source Control, with a card for each attached repo, and the branch name in Source Control switches or creates a branch in place.
- 💬 **Ask without derailing a chat:** In Chat UI, `/btw` asks a side question in a fork beside the chat while the original keeps running, and `/fork` branches from the latest response. Chats that open or push to a pull request show a short line when its CI passes or fails.
- 🎙️ **Dictate from anywhere:** Phones can turn speech into text on the device (iPhone on iOS 26 or later, and Android), with the computer as fallback. The computer, phones and web client can dictate at the same time, and on-device dictation runs in its own process, so a speech engine crash or hang no longer takes Orca down.
- 📱 **A phone that holds on to your work:** Chat sends queue while the desktop is unreachable and go out in order when it's back. Chat drafts, attachments, unsaved file edits and automation drafts survive the app being killed, and screen

Browse plugins →

Docs →

Also in the box:

  • Drag Files to Agents: drag files from the explorer, or images from your desktop, straight into an agent's prompt.
  • Jump Anywhere: one shortcut jumps to any workspace or tab across every repo and host.
  • Rich Previews: open images, PDFs, and Markdown right in the workspace, next to the agent that made them.
  • Mobile Emulator: run an iOS Simulator or Android emulator beside your agent, and let it tap, type, and check its own work.
  • Dictation: press a shortcut and talk. Orca types what you say into the agent's prompt or terminal.
  • Usage & Accounts: see how much of your agent limits you've used and when they reset, and switch accounts without logging out.
  • Automations: schedule prompts to run on any repo: nightly dependency bumps, weekly triage, flaky-test sweeps.
  • Computer Use: when there's no CLI or API, agents can see and drive desktop apps and external browsers.
  • And many, many more: we ship daily, so this list is perpetually behind. The changelog is the real feature list.

Supported Agents

Works with any CLI agent — if it runs in a terminal, it runs in Orca.

Claude Code   Codex   Grok   Cursor   GitHub Copilot   Muse   DeepSeek Harness   ZCode   OpenCode   MiMo Code   Amp   OpenClaude   Antigravity   Pi   oh-my-pi   Hermes Agent   Devin   Goose   Auggie   Autohand Code   Charm   Cline   CodeBuddy   Codebuff   Freebuff   Command Code   Continue   Droid   Kilocode   Kimi   Kiro   Mistral Vibe   Qwen Code   Rovo Dev   + any CLI agent

Install

Desktop — macOS, Windows, Linux

  • Download from orca.dev
  • Or grab a build directly: macOS Apple Silicon · macOS Intel · Windows (.exe) · Linux AppImage · All builds

Or via a package manager:

# macOS (Homebrew)
# Always use the full name; bare `orca` is an unrelated Plotly cask.
brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca
# Upgrade an existing install
brew upgrade --cask stablyai/orca/orca
# Release candidates (conflicts with the stable cask; uninstall it first)
brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca@rc

# Arch Linux (AUR) — or stably-orca-git to build from source
yay -S stably-orca-bin

Mobile App — iOS, Android

Pair with your desktop app to monitor and steer your agents from your phone.

  • iOS: Download on the App Store
  • Android: Download APK · Install guide

Community & Support

  • Discord: Join the community on Discord.

  • Twitter / X: Follow @orca_build for updates and announcements.

  • WeChat: Scan to join an Orca community WeChat group.

  • Feedback & Ideas: We ship fast. Missing something? Request a new feature.

  • Privacy: See the privacy & telemetry docs for what anonymous usage data Orca collects and how to opt out.

  • Show Support: Star this repo to follow along with our daily ships.

Developing

Want to contribute or run locally? See our CONTRIBUTING.md guide.

Signed Builds

Windows code signing sponsored/provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation.

License

Orca is free and open source under the MIT License.
